$comment: Rhymvex locales. Canonical source consumed by web/ via scripts/sync-content.mjs. One URL segment carries the LANGUAGE. The pricing deliberately does not: a currency is a preference the visitor makes and it is remembered in a cookie, so English can be read in pounds or in yen. `currency` here is only the fallback for a visitor who has never chosen, which is what keeps /en-GB priced in pounds on a first visit. This is keyed by BCP-47 language tag, not market code: en-GB and en-US are the same language, ar and th-TH are different languages in different scripts. `default` is served at the un-prefixed URL so every existing link keeps working. Budget bands are NOT here: they belong to the currency and live in content/currencies.json. Adding a language is one entry here plus one catalogue in content/messages/; adding a currency is one entry there. Copy rules still apply in every language: no em dashes in prose, no (X, not Y) constructions, one triad per page maximum.
